transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Product), Rajiv Malhotra (Zenith), Sofia Alvarez (Zenith), Tom Reed (Zenith), Nadia Khan (Zenith Legal)
Deck: https://redwood.example.com/deck/zenith-data-controls

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the Zenith account, Arjun is our SE and Lena is product. We'll demo how request storage toggles and PII redaction work across the API and Console.

[00:01:12] Rajiv: Thanks. High level: our main ask is we need to be sure sensitive customer prompts never land in log storage by default, but we also want to preserve a short audit trail for debugging. Interested in retention windows and how redaction works.

[00:02:05] Arjun: Great, I'll share my screen. Quick note, transcription may show a few words wrong — I tend to talk fast. Starting at the Console -> Settings -> Data controls panel.

[00:03:01] Arjun: (screen) So first toggle is "Request Storage" — default is on for Hosted, off for Private. You can set it to Never, On 24h, 7d, 30d, or Custom. If you pick Never, requests are not written to persistent request store. Temp in-flight caching for KV and batching still happens in memory.

[00:04:20] Sofia: When you say "not written to persistent store" does that include audit logs? We need an immutable audit trail for certain ops.

[00:04:40] Arjun: Good question. There are two layers: the request store (payloads) and the audit log (event metadata). If you set Request Storage to Never, payloads are not persisted but audit events (timestamps, route, model id, token counts) still flow to audit logging which can be configured to forward to your SIEM. We can turn off payload-level entries in audit too if required.

[00:05:50] Tom: What about PII redaction — is that pre-send or post-store? We have cases where redaction must be applied before any disk writes by policy.

[00:06:15] Arjun: Redwood supports two modes: pre-ingest redaction and post-processing redaction. In pre-ingest, the PII filter runs inline in the gateway before any persistent storage. Patterns and ML detectors detect e.g. SSNs, credit card numbers, and certain named entity types. Post-process redaction can run off a job that rewrites stored requests. Pre-ingest is recommended for strict compliance.

[00:07:30] Rajiv: Is the pre-ingest detector deterministic? We worry about false positives removing content we need for debugging.

[00:07:52] Lena: We provide a confidence threshold and a review mode. By default, redaction replaces the token span with "[REDACTED]" and tags the event. You can set a buffer window where only high-confidence matches are redacted automatically, lower confidence flagged for manual review in the audit UI.

[00:09:05] Sofia: For EU data residency — can we keep payloads within EU regions and still use Hosted?

[00:09:25] Maya: Yes, Hosted has region pinning. You can pin the customer's tenant to eu-west-1 and control retention policies per-tenant. For extra assurance we also offer Redwood Private VPC where the control plane is customer managed.

[00:10:40] Rajiv: How does KMS integration look? Keys must be customer-managed.

[00:10:55] Arjun: We support BYOK via KMS/HSM. You bring the key; Redwood wraps request payloads with envelope encryption. Audit logs show key id references but not raw key material. Key rotation is supported; we log rotation events.

[00:12:20] Nadia: From legal side: we need documented proof that payloads can be purged on request within 24 hours and that backups will not retain them.

[00:12:42] Maya: We have a documented data deletion flow and we can provide evidence of purge workflows. For backups we keep separate policies — with Request Storage set to Never, payloads are not present to back up; if you run with retention windows we have scheduled purges and a backup exclusion list. We'll send the runbook.

[00:14:10] Tom: Slight tangent — does Optimize's batching and caching create any copying of requests to disk? We're concerned about KV cache and whether it persists sensitive prefixes.

[00:14:36] Arjun: Optimize/Serving runtime uses in-memory KV cache. By default it's memory-only; however some deployments (Dedicated with heavy burst) might spill to local SSD for performance. That behavior is configurable and you can disable persistent spill. Also, the Console shows per-route cache/no-cache controls.

[00:16:05] Rajiv: Ok, show us the API level for toggles — we want infra automation.

[00:16:30] Arjun: Sure: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data-controls with JSON body. Example: {"request_storage":"24h", "pre_ingest_redaction": true, "redaction_threshold": 0.95}. (note: transcription, braces shown). You can set KMS key id as well.

[00:17:45] Rajiv: Are there SDKs to flip these programmatically?

[00:18:02] Maya: Yes, SDKs in Python/TS expose the same calls; we can share a terraform provider snippet for IaC.

[00:19:10] Sofia: If we toggle request storage off, will we lose the ability to replay requests for debugging?

[00:19:30] Arjun: Yes, persistent request replay won't be available. We recommend capturing minimal debug context to audit logs and enabling a 24h buffer in Request Storage during initial rollout so you can debug incidents then tighten to Never.

[00:21:05] Rajiv: Can the redaction be tuned to keep named entities like product codes? We need certain tokens to remain for downstream ML training.

[00:21:28] Lena: You can provide allowlists and entity-specific rules. The redaction engine supports custom regex, ML rules, and allowlist overrides per route. We log the rule matches in a metadata-only stream if you need to retain non-sensitive labels.

[00:22:55] Tom: What about retention windows on embeddings? We plan to store embeddings for search but embeddings derived from PII-containing prompts are disallowed.

[00:23:15] Arjun: We distinguish derived assets. Embeddings and fine-tune artifacts are separate storage classes. You can configure a transform step that strips PII before embedding generation; the Console has pipeline presets for that.

[00:24:40] Rajiv: Show us an example audit export — need to ingest to Splunk.

[00:24:55] Arjun: Export can be JSON lines with schema: event_ts, tenant_id, route, op, token_count, redaction_flags. Payload hashes are included if payloads are stored; otherwise it's null. (brief pause while he navigates)

[00:26:10] Speaker 1: [inaudible] — sounds like the policy config has a lot of knobs, how long to set this up?

[00:26:25] Maya: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: Week 1 onboard + sandbox, Week 2 run redaction tests and tweak rules, Week 3 run pilot traffic and collect metrics.

[00:27:40] Sofia: About metrics — what impact on latency and cost for pre-ingest redaction?

[00:27:58] Arjun: Pre-ingest redaction adds CPU at the gateway — small ms-level. For high throughput you can offload detection to an isolated redaction service or use sampling for lower cost. We can run benchmarks in your pilot to measure exact ms impact.

[00:29:10] Rajiv: Any vendor lock-in concerns if we later move from Hosted to Dedicated? Will redaction rules migrate?

[00:29:30] Lena: Rules are stored as tenant config (JSON) and can be exported. Moving to Dedicated keeps the same configs. For Private on-prem there are extra deployment steps but no rule conversion needed.

[00:30:50] Nadia: Legal also wants a clear SLA on purge times and notarized deletion logs for audits.

[00:31:10] Maya: We can include purge certificates in enterprise contracts and log proof-of-deletion events. We'll add that to the packet we send.

[00:33:00] Rajiv: Could you walk through a quick live toggle? Turn off request storage for a test tenant and show the UI flow.

[00:33:18] Arjun: (clicks) Console -> Tenants -> Zenith-POC -> Data Controls. Toggle set to 24h. Changing to Never warns you that historical payloads will be inaccessible. Confirm — policy applied. Backend shows an event at 2025-06-18T23:33:20Z.

[00:35:05] Tom: I see the audit row but the payload hash is null, good.

[00:35:40] Rajiv: Can we get an API call to query current config?

[00:35:58] Arjun: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data-controls returns your JSON config and last_applied_ts. We'll share curl examples.

[00:37:20] Sofia: A quick note on SSO and RBAC — we need role separation for Dev vs Security so only Security can change redaction thresholds.

[00:37:45] Maya: Console has RBAC; roles can be mapped to SAML groups. We'll provide a recommended role matrix for you to review.

[00:39:10] Rajiv: If we run the pilot, what logs will you need from our side to validate redaction coverage?

[00:39:30] Arjun: We ask for 100-200 sample prompts (anonymized) and acceptance criteria: percent redacted, false positive rate under X, and performance delta. We can also run synthetic augmentations to stress-test detectors.

[00:41:00] Rajiv: Sounds good. Any gotchas?

[00:41:12] Arjun: Watch out for prefix caching: if prompts reuse shared prefixes with PII in non-stored routes there is potential for leakage if you enable persistent KV spilling. Keep spill disabled or ensure prefix masking. Also ensure downstream logging from client apps doesn't duplicate payloads outside Redwood.

[00:42:35] Maya: Quick recap — we showed Console toggles, API calls, pre-ingest redaction modes, KMS/BYOK, audit exports, and region pinning.

[00:43:10] Rajiv: Next steps from Zenith: Sofia will send regulatory list, Rajiv to confirm pilot dataset, Nadia needs contract language for purge certificates.

[00:44:00] Maya: Great, we'll send the security packet, the terraform snippet, and a short demo video of toggles. We'll aim to have materials in 48 hours.

[00:45:20] Lena: I'll also include a sample redaction ruleset and example Splunk ingestion mapping.

[00:46:10] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.

[00:46:30] (meeting ends)
